provenance_policy: Requester's updated rule: provenance does NOT matter. Official show/movie scenes, fan FUI recreations, studio VFX breakdowns, motion-graphics reels and UI concept animations are all acceptable. Ranking is by DESIGN CONCEPT quality (waveforms, holographic gauges, animated grids, status systems) plus influence on UI culture; each entry notes which YouTube source type is likely best.
covered: Star Trek (TNG/DS9/VOY LCARS, TOS bridge panels, Enterprise-E schematics)
Battlestar Galactica (DRADIS tactical grids - fan recreations)
Ghost in the Shell SAC (green CRT terminals)
PREVIOUSLY FAILED (retry opportunities, not counted as covered): 2001 A Space Odyssey, Psycho-Pass, Ready Player One

ark_interpretation: I chose 'The Ark' (2023 Syfy series, created by Dean Devlin) over 'ARK: The Animated Series' (2024, based on ARK: Survival Evolved). Reason: The Ark is set almost entirely aboard the starship Ark One and has a standing bridge/command deck with navigation, hull-breach, FTL and surveillance console scenes in nearly every episode - high scene availability and a coherent monochromatic console language (production designer Randal Groves, 'Star Wars meets SpaceX' brief). ARK: The Animated Series is prehistoric-island survival drama with essentially no consoles - only occasional glowing green body-scan panels and arm-implant devices, which fails the visual-density bar. Caveat: if the requester meant the ARK video game, ARK: Survival Evolved has a famous, highly distinct 'Specimen Implant' forearm display plus engram/pause-menu UI - that would be the strongest 'ARK' reference of the three, and under the new provenance rule a fan FUI recreation of the implant HUD would be perfectly acceptable. Note also that under the new 'design concepts over official footage' rule, The Ark (2023) drops relative to other entries: it has no FUI reel, no breakdowns and no fan recreation scene, so its only sources are dull official clips - it stays ranked last in the gap list.
